Data Analysis

Data Collection

I have collected the data using the Spotify Music Analysis Server. Doing that I created a dataset from scratch. I only included album songs

Data Importing

To import the data I have used the following function, along with getting my packages in order.

library(ggplot2) #these are the packages I used for my analysis
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

PBData <- read.csv("pb.csv.csv") # stored all of my data under this name

You can take a look at some of the data over here

PBData |> dplyr::slice_sample(n=5) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
Song Acousticness Danceability Energy Instrumentalness Liveness Loudness Speechiness Tempo Valence album_name

Data Preparation

I really didn’t need to mess with the data in any way, as I have all collected it by hand.

Valence/Energy Analysis by Album

I was curious to see in which sector of the graph would Panda Bear songs prevalently lie in(Angry/Joyful/Peaceful/Sad)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(PBData, aes(x = Energy, 
                   y = Valence, 
                   color = album_name)) +
  
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 1) + 
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "black") +
  
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5,
             linetype = "dashed",
             color = "black") +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c(  #colors were chosen on visibility
    "Reset" = "orange",
    "Tomboy" = "pink",
    "Person Pitch" = "darkblue",
    "Buoys" = "purple",
    "PBVSTGR" = "green",
    "Sinister Grift" = "red",
    "Young Prayer" = "black"
  )) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  
  labs(title = "Panda Bear Songs: Energy vs Valence",
       x = "Energy (Calm → Energetic)",
       y = "Valence (Sad → Happy)",
       color = "Album")

While seeing all the songs at once on a scatter chart was cool, I wanted to break it down further for Energy and Valence using Histograms and Boxplots

ggplot(PBData, aes(x = Energy)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..),
                 fill = "lightblue",
                 color = "black",
                 bins = 15) +
  geom_density(fill = "#FF6666",
               alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(album_name ~ .) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Energy",
       x = "Energy",
       y = "Density")

It seems that Panda Bear’s early work is more mellow

library(ggplot2)

PBData$album_name <- as.factor(PBData$album_name)

ggplot(PBData, aes(x = album_name, y = Valence)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Album name",
       y = "Valence")

Most Positive/Negative Tracks

I was curious to find out what would Panda Bears five most positive and negative tracks be. For that I used the following code(positive first, negative after)

PBData |>
  slice_max(Valence, n = 5) |>
  select(Song, album_name, Valence) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
Song album_name Valence
Just as Well Sinister Grift 0.94
Untitled 5 Young Prayer 0.93
Ferry Lady Sinister Grift 0.92
Gettin to the Point Reset 0.90
Ends Meet Sinister Grift 0.85 
PBData |>
  slice_min(Valence, n = 5) |>
  select(Song, album_name, Valence) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
Song album_name Valence
Shadow Of The Colossus PBVSTGR 0.00
Untitled 4 Young Prayer 0.03
Untitled 7 Young Prayer 0.03
Davy Jones’ Locker PBVSTGR 0.04
Drone Tomboy 0.04

The Spotify Music Analysis Server does not know that those are interludes. Let’s fix that

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

PBData |>
  arrange(Valence) |>        
  slice(5:9) |>              # skip first 4 interludes, take next 5 tracks
  select(Song, album_name, Valence) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
Song album_name Valence
Drone Tomboy 0.04
Comfy In Nautica Person Pitch 0.04
Elegy for Noah Lou Sinister Grift 0.04
Benfica Tomboy 0.04
Untitled 8 Young Prayer 0.05

PBData |>

Song album_name Danceability
